goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `pathFor()` in adapters/embedding.js.es6 returns `/admin/customize/embedding` ignoring the id, so host.save PUTs to a no-op update and changes are never persisted

adjudication.rationale: The adapter in `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` only affects the `embedding` model requests (GET/PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding`), and the Rails routes explicitly define that endpoint without an `:id`, so ignoring an id there is consistent with the backend. The persistence of hosts is handled via `host.save(props)` on the `embeddable-host` record, which uses the `embeddable-host` model/adapter and is routed to `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`resources :embeddable_hosts`). So the claim that `host.save` PUTs to `/admin/customize/embedding` (a no-op update) and therefore never persists changes is a misread of the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `destroyRecord()` DELETEs to `/admin/customize/embedding`, which has no route, so deletion of existing hosts fails

adjudication.rationale: The `destroyRecord()` call is invoked on `this.get('host')`, which is an `embeddable-host` record (created via `this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')`). The diff adds `embeddable-host` to `ADMIN_MODELS`, causing the REST adapter to use the `/admin/` base path for that type, and `config/routes.rb` defines `resources :embeddable_hosts` under the admin namespace, providing DELETE `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id`. The `/admin/customize/embedding` path is only returned by the newly added `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` adapter for the `embedding` model, not for `embeddable-host` deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embedding serializer uses `embed: :ids` sending only host ids; controller never side-loads embeddable_hosts records, so the admin page renders no rows

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads how `embed: :ids` works in this codebase. `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which in Discourse’s serialization convention means the main payload includes `embeddable_host_ids` *and* side-loads the referenced `embeddable_hosts` records at the top level. The controller’s `show` action renders `@embedding` with `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`, so there is data to serialize and side-load. Additionally, the diff explicitly updates the JS store hydration logic to handle `*_ids` plural keys and convert them into the pluralized relationship (`embeddable_hosts`) by looking up the sideloaded records, indicating this is an intended and supported pattern. Therefore, it’s not verifiable from the diff that “no rows render” due to missing sideloading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates raw site-setting host text into SQL, raising on values needing escaping and wedging the upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration reads the `embeddable_hosts` site_setting value, splits it into `h`, and then runs `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. This directly interpolates raw setting text into SQL without quoting/escaping via the connection adapter. If any configured host line contains a single quote or other SQL-significant characters (even accidentally), the migration SQL will break and can halt the upgrade; it also creates a SQL-injection surface using admin-controlled data.

Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

`Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op that just re-renders, so the save button does nothing while appearing to succeed

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` indeed just re-renders the serialized embedding object and does not persist any changes. However, the admin UI added here (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) does not include any "save" button or call to the controller’s `saveChanges` action; the only actions exposed are per-host save/delete handled via `EmbeddableHost#save` / `destroyRecord` hitting `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`. So the claim that "the save button does nothing" is not verifiable from this diff—the only visible saving functionality is on individual hosts, and that does perform writes. The no-op `update` action looks unused/placeholder rather than a demonstrated defect in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? performs an uncached DB query on every embed request, a hot path hit on every page view of embedded comment iframes

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff replaces the prior `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` check (string parsing in memory) with `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which calls `record_for_host` and does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. This is an uncached DB lookup executed in hot paths like `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (runs per embed iframe request) and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Nothing in the diff adds memoization or caching, so it is verifiably a per-request DB query regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing index on host column for the lower(host) lookup in record_for_host, causing a seq scan per request

adjudication.rationale: The new `embeddable_hosts` table migration (`20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) creates columns but adds no index on `host`. Runtime checks call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (used in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), which performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. Without an appropriate index (typically a functional index on `lower(host)` in Postgres, not just a plain `host` index), this lookup will require a sequential scan as the table grows, and it can be executed per embed request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding loads all hosts unbounded with no limit/pagination

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding`, the code does `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` which is indeed an unbounded query. However, this is for an admin-only “Embedding” settings page whose purpose is to list/edit all allowed hosts; no requirement for pagination/limit is implied by the diff, and the data set is typically expected to be small. So while the statement is factually accurate, it’s a speculative scalability concern rather than a clear defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates host values directly into SQL, which can break on hosts containing quotes — should sanitize/quote before insert
record_for_host returns false vs nil inconsistently with host_allowed? usage

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` returns `false` for invalid/missing URIs, but all shown call sites handle that safely: `host_allowed?` uses `record_for_host(host).present?` where `false.present?` and `nil.present?` are both `false`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` where `false.try(...)` returns `nil` in Rails. There’s no verifiable incorrect behavior introduced by returning `false` vs `nil` based on the provided code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingSerializer#embeddable_hosts serialized as IDs only but client expects hydrated host objects; should use embed: :objects
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting was never saved (nil-safe handling missing)

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```rb
category_id = execute("SELECT ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If the `site_settings` row for `embed_category` does not exist (e.g., the setting was never saved / created), `execute(...)` returns an empty result set, so `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`. The later fallback `if category_id == 0` is never reached because the exception happens first. This is a real, verifiable crash path introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroy action calls .destroy on possibly-nil record, raising NoMethodError (500) instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `host.destroy`. If no record matches the given `:id`, `host` will be `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError` (500) instead of returning a 404/not-found response. (The same nil-risk also exists in `#update` via `save_host(host)`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /customize/embedding update action is a no-op that re-renders serializer without persisting, falsely reporting success

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads params or persists any changes (it also builds `@embedding` from `OpenStruct` in `fetch_embedding`). Yet routes expose `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, and the Ember controller calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, so a PUT will return a successful serialized response without actually updating anything.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host assumes params[:embeddable_host] exists, causing NoMethodError instead of 400 for missing params

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` without checking that `params[:embeddable_host]` is present. If a client sends a malformed request (or omits the root key), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil` and `nil[:host]` will raise a `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 rather than a clean 4xx response. This is a real, verifiable failure mode in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates host values directly into raw SQL INSERT; single quotes break the migration

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. If any existing `embeddable_hosts` setting line contains a single quote (or other SQL-special chars), the generated SQL becomes invalid and the migration will fail. Because the value comes from `site_settings` and is not escaped/parameterized, this is a concrete correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host and vice versa

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (with `host` and `category`), while the new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the former category-related fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`). So the fabricator definitions are indeed swapped relative to the filenames, which is a verifiable defect in the diff (and could break any code that requires fabricator files by name rather than glob-loading all fabricators).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration builds SQL via string interpolation of unvalidated site setting values, allowing quote breakage/injection; should use sanitized/bound params

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration reads the existing `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it, and then builds an INSERT via string interpolation:

```rb
records.each do |h|
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
```

`h` comes from the database and is not escaped/sanitized. If the stored setting contains a quote (e.g. `eviltrout.com'`), the SQL will break and the migration can fail; with certain DB adapters/configurations it could also permit SQL injection/multi-statement execution. Using bound params/quoting (e.g. `quote(h)` / `exec_insert` / `sanitize_sql_array`) would avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client delete() has no error handling on destroyRecord (no .catch(popupAjaxError)), leaving the user with no feedback on failure

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` without any `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which ends with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the server delete fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and there is no user-facing error feedback, so the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host port/case mismatch: hosts saved with a port (permitted by validation regex) can never match URI(referer).host, breaking embedding for those sites

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: `EmbeddableHost` allows storing hosts with an explicit port (`validates_format_of` permits `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` and the `before_validation` normalization strips scheme and path but does not remove the port). However `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the referer/url with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which *never includes the port* (port is in `uri.port`). The lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` therefore compares e.g. stored `example.com:8080` against lookup key `example.com`, so those records will never match and embedding will be rejected for port-specific entries. (Case handling may also be problematic because only the DB side is lowercased, but the port mismatch is clearly verifiable from the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: saveChanges issues an empty PUT to a no-op update action with no error handling, causing silent failures and a dead/misleading control

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, the `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty payload and no `.then/.catch` handling. On the server side, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (new file) does not persist any changes; it simply re-renders the serialized `@embedding` (which is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). So if `saveChanges` is triggered, it will issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` that is effectively a no-op and provides no explicit error/feedback handling in this action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation crashes on nil host via self.host.sub! (NoMethodError), and sub! can return nil leaving field untouched; should use assignment with a nil guard
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: the before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! and will raise NoMethodError when host is nil. Extra notes about sub! returning nil are additional but don’t change the underlying issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import passes the raw article URL to record_for_host while ensure_embeddable uses referer; unparsable URLs silently yield nil category, regressing the previous embed_category fallback
category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have swapped contents due to copy/paste mistake

Conversely, the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the full set of `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. adjudication_records.issue_text: New Admin::EmbeddableHostsController CRUD endpoints have zero behavioral test coverage (validation failures, category_id fallback, 404 handling, staff-only authorization)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` with create/update/destroy behavior (`save_host`, category_id fallback to `uncategorized_category_id`, and no nil/404 handling when `EmbeddableHost.where(...).first` returns nil). adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test doesn't actually exercise the removed embeddable-host guard condition

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Topic#expandable_first_post?` changed from checking `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` to no longer checking any “embeddable host” condition. However, the diff snippet for `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` is truncated right after the start of the `describe "expandable_first_post?"` block and does not include any test named “is false if embeddable_host is blank” (or similar). Since the referenced spec assertion is not verifiably present in the provided diff, and the finding is about test coverage rather than a demonstrated defect in the changed code, this is not a real, confirmable problem grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import lacks coverage for the case when no embeddable host matches, causing topic to land in uncategorized category

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `TopicEmbed.import` to set `category: eh.try(:category_id)` where `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`. If no matching `EmbeddableHost` exists, `eh` is `nil` and the category argument becomes `nil`, but the code path that calls embedding import is now guarded elsewhere: both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` reject requests unless `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` is true. So, under normal operation, `TopicEmbed.import` should not be reached with a non-matching host. The proposed finding is primarily about missing test coverage, and it also assumes the post will land in Uncategorized, which is not directly verifiable from this diff (it could also error or be handled by PostCreator). Therefore it does not describe a clear, verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host exact match (lower(host) = ?) subdomain/port behavior is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which parses a URL via `URI(...)` and matches `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Store hydration edge cases untested: empty color_ids array and unknown sub-type id references

adjudication_records.issue_text: No client test for new admin embedding UI (embeddable-host save/cancel/delete actions and category-chooser wiring)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, making file names misleading

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines `Fabricator(:category)` and instead defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category` (and related) fabricators that used to live in `category_fabricator.rb`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates unsanitized site setting values into SQL, breaking on quotes and storing hosts with http:// prefixes raw so record_for_host never matches them post-upgrade

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. This is not quoted/escaped, so a host value containing a `'` will break the SQL (and it also creates an injection vector from stored site_settings data). Also, `h` is inserted exactly as it appears in the old `embeddable_hosts` site setting (which could include `http://...` or paths). Because this bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization, those rows can be stored with prefixes/paths, but `record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` (e.g. `discourse.org`), so migrated rows like `http://discourse.org` would not match and embedding would be incorrectly rejected post-upgrade.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration raises NoMethodError via [0]['id'] when embed_category/uncategorized_category_id rows are absent from site_settings

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` to fetch the `embed_category` setting via an INNER JOIN. If the `site_settings` row for `embed_category` is missing (which is plausible in a fresh install given this diff removes `embed_category` from `config/site_settings.yml`), `execute(...)` returns an empty result and `[0]` is `nil`, causing `NoMethodError` when indexing `['id']`. The same unguarded pattern exists for `uncategorized_category_id` (`execute(...)[0]['value']`) if that row were missing. There is no presence check before indexing `[0]` for these queries, so the finding is a real, verifiable failure mode introduced/present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController destroy/update crash with NoMethodError (500 instead of 404) when host lookup returns nil
Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that re-renders unchanged embedding while client wires saveChanges() to a useless PUT

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and does not read params or persist any changes (it’s effectively identical to `#show`). On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` via the new adapter. That PUT will be a no-op on the server and returns unchanged data, so the finding is verifiably accurate based on the added code/routes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OpenStruct used as pseudo-model in embedding controller leaks across serializer boundary; Embedding resource never persisted but treated as REST resource with unused PUT route

adjudication.rationale:
The diff intentionally models “embedding” as a synthetic resource: `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts`, and the serializer just reads `id` plus the `embeddable_hosts` collection. That usage is compatible with the serializer (it only needs method accessors) and does not demonstrate a serializer-boundary “leak” or a concrete bug.

It’s true that a PUT route and `#update` action exist but `#update` is a no-op (it only re-renders the same serialization) and the client template shown doesn’t call `saveChanges` anyway. That’s dead/placeholder API surface, but not a verifiable correctness/security defect introduced by the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostSerializer reimplements default attribute accessors for id/host/category_id — pure duplication

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb`, the serializer declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` and then defines `def id; object.id; end`, `def host; object.host; end`, and `def category_id; object.category_id; end`. In typical Rails/AMS-style serializers, these explicit methods are unnecessary because the attribute declaration will already read the corresponding fields from `object`. However, this is a redundancy/cleanup issue, not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff—the code will behave the same either way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation calls sub! on nil host when host is blank, producing 500 instead of validation error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` block unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., a request omits `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, or any code constructs `EmbeddableHost.new` without `host`), `sub!` will raise `NoMethodError`, causing a 500 before the `validates_format_of :host` can add a validation error. There is no nil-guard in the callback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Underscore→hyphen rewrite in shared REST basePath changes basePath resolution for every REST model, a global behavior change to fix a per-model routing concern

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath(store, type)` changes the *admin-model detection* check from `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type)` to `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_','-'))`. This does not change `basePath` resolution for “every REST model” in general: it only changes behavior when (a) `type` contains an underscore and (b) the underscore→dash transformed name matches an entry in `ADMIN_MODELS`. For all other models, the method still returns `"/"` as before. Also, the change appears intentionally targeted to make models like `embeddable-host` (and possibly `site-customization`) be recognized as admin models. The proposed finding is therefore overstated and not a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side category assignment in embeddable-host.js.es6 duplicates server fallback logic for blank category_id, creating two sources of truth

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6`, the client always sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and does not implement any fallback for a blank/null category. The server-side fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` exists only in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`. So there is no duplicated fallback logic on the client; the diff shows only one fallback source (server). (There may be a separate potential mismatch after save if `categoryId` is null, but that’s different from “duplicating fallback logic”.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting is unset ('' default), since JOIN returns no rows and execute(...)[0] is nil before the fallback check

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb: `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the JOIN query returns at least one row. If the `site_settings` row for `embed_category` is missing or doesn’t match any category name (e.g., unset/blank), `execute(...)[0]` will be `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection/breakage via unescaped string interpolation of embeddable_hosts setting values into VALUES SQL in backfill
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying security issue: building an SQL statement by interpolating embeddable host values directly into the query string (e.g., '#{h}' / VALUES clause) without proper escaping or parameter binding, which can lead to SQL injection or query breakage. The candidate phrasing matches the golden concern even if it doesn’t name the exact file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfilled hosts bypass EmbeddableHost validation and normalization; stored values with paths/schemes will never match record_for_host, silently breaking embedding after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` backfills from the old `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` by directly executing raw SQL inserts: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` with `h` taken verbatim from the setting lines. This bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization (`sub!` stripping `http(s)://` and paths) and its format validation. After the change, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`, which parses the incoming URL/referer and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the backfilled DB value includes a scheme or path (e.g. `https://example.com/1234`, which the previous SiteSetting logic explicitly handled), it will be stored as-is and will not match `uri.host` (`example.com`), silently breaking embedding/whitelisting for those upgraded configs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DELETE of site_settings rows inside change migration is destructive and non-reversible; migration not safely re-runnable when DDL is non-transactional

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration uses `def change` and performs data-changing SQL via `execute`, including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Because this is in a `change` migration with irreversible raw SQL, Rails cannot automatically reverse it on rollback (it would be an irreversible migration / the deleted rows can’t be restored). Additionally, if the migration errors after the DELETE (or if DDL isn’t fully transactional in the target DB), it can leave the system in a partially-migrated state with the old settings removed, making a retry/rollback unsafe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator definitions swapped between category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, breaking all specs that use Fabricate(:category)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move the `Fabricator(:category)` (and related category fabricators) out of `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` into the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, while `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. However, Fabrication loads all files under `spec/fabricators` (typically via a Dir glob in `spec_helper`), and fabricator names—not filenames—determine `Fabricate(:category)` availability. Since `Fabricator(:category)` is still defined in the diff (just in a different file), specs calling `Fabricate(:category)` are not verifiably broken by this change based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy return 500 (NoMethodError) instead of 404 for unknown ids since nil host is passed to save_host/destroy
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes that update/destroy for unknown IDs result in a NoMethodError because the host lookup returns nil and is then passed to save_host/destroy, which matches the golden issue about not validating existence of the EmbeddableHost record before calling methods on it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host uses lower(host) = ? without downcasing the bound host from URI.host, causing case-sensitive matching failures
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that record_for_host lowercases the column in the SQL comparison but does not lowercase/normalize the input host parameter, so mixed-case hosts may not match as intended in a case-insensitive comparison.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that saves nothing, making the PUT /customize/embedding endpoint misleading dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` and never reads `params` or persists any changes (and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). On the client, `admin-embedding` controller calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding`, but that endpoint will always be a no-op. This makes the PUT route/action misleading/dead with respect to saving state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration raises NoMethodError when the embed_category setting lookup returns no matching row (nil [0]['id']), halting the deploy

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does:

category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i

If there is no matching site_settings row/value for embed_category (common if the setting was never set), the SQL result will be empty, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError before the later fallback `if category_id == 0` can run. This would halt the migration/deploy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates host values directly into SQL, so legacy values containing quotes break the migration and it's a raw injection vector from previously-admin-controlled data

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds raw SQL via string interpolation:

```rb
records.each do |h|
  execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
end
```

`h` comes from the existing `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines). If any legacy host value contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), the migration SQL will break. Because it is inserted unescaped into a SQL string, it is also a classic SQL injection vector from previously stored data (even if that data was typically admin-controlled). This is a verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration has no rollback path: raw execute inserts aren't reversible by change, leaving the DB half-migrated on mid-migration failure

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` but performs multiple raw `execute` statements (SELECTs, INSERTs, and a DELETE from `site_settings`). Rails cannot automatically reverse `execute` calls, so rolling back this migration would be irreversible (typically raising `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration`) and it also deletes old settings (`embeddable_hosts`, `embed_category`) without any down-path to restore them. The specific claim about being “half-migrated on mid-migration failure” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff (migrations often run in a transaction), but the lack of a rollback path is a real issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are accidentally swapped, causing silent test-suite breakage risk

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines `:category` (it now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the old category-related fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, etc.). That is an objective swap/misplacement of fabricator definitions relative to filenames, which can cause test breakage if any specs or helpers require fabricator files by name (or if load order/partial loading occurs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a fake save: it does nothing except re-serialize the unchanged OpenStruct, so the client reports 'saved' while persisting nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not read any params or persist anything; it simply re-renders `@embedding`, which is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding` from `EmbeddableHost.all`. So a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` will succeed and return serialized data without saving changes. Additionally, the client controller defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, meaning there is at least some client code path intended to invoke this no-op update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController update/destroy crash with 500 (NoMethodError on nil) for missing/already-deleted ids instead of graceful 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` but do not handle the case where no record is found. In `update`, `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` and crash with `NoMethodError` if `host` is `nil`. In `destroy`, `host.destroy` will also crash if `host` is `nil`. This would yield a 500 for missing/already-deleted IDs rather than a graceful 404/not-found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host never checks host.persisted?, so a PUT to a nonexistent id silently creates a host with a client-supplied id

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `save_host(host)`. If the ID does not exist, `host` will be `nil` and `save_host` will raise (it calls `host.host = ...`), rather than silently creating a new record. There is no path here that instantiates a new `EmbeddableHost` with a client-supplied `id`; only `#create` uses `EmbeddableHost.new` without setting an ID from params. The real issue is lack of a not-found check/404 handling, but the proposed finding’s “silently creates a host with a client-supplied id” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host compares URI(host).host (port stripped) against stored hosts that may include a port, so records like example.com:8080 can never match any referer

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbeddableHost` the `host` field validation explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` cleanup strips scheme and path but does not strip a port, so a record like `example.com:8080` can be saved. However `record_for_host` does `uri = URI(host)` and then `host = uri.host`, and `URI#host` returns the hostname without the port. The subsequent lookup `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` will compare `"example.com"` against the stored `"example.com:8080"`, which will never match. Therefore port-qualified allowed-host records cannot work as intended, and referers on non-default ports will also not be matchable against stored `host:port` entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host does lower(host) = ? but nothing downcases host on save (including migration-inserted legacy values), so mixed-case stored hosts never match
Store _hydrateEmbedded unconditionally deletes xxx_ids keys even when the sub-type can't be resolved, producing arrays of undefined and destroying original ids

adjudication.rationale:
In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` was changed to also match `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the plural (`m[2]` truthy) branch it does:

- `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))`
- `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`
- `delete obj[k]`

Unlike the singular `_id` branch, it deletes the original `*_ids` key unconditionally, even if `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined` for some/all ids. That can yield an array containing `undefined` entries and loses the original ids array, making the object unrecoverable for later hydration/resolution. This is a real behavioral/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost before_validation crashes with NoMethodError on nil host (e.g. API POST missing host param) instead of returning a validation error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` block unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)`. If `host` is `nil`, this raises `NoMethodError` before validations can add an error. This can occur if a create/update request omits `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` (see `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, which assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` with no presence check). Thus the code can crash instead of returning a validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroyRecord/deleteHost has no error handling: on failure the row stays with no user feedback (no popupAjaxError)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` with no `.catch(...)` and no `popupAjaxError` (unlike the `save()` action, which does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the server-side `DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id` fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the user gets no feedback; the row remains in the table without an error popup. This is directly verifiable from the diff.
